name: SPIN Selling
origin: Neil Rackham, based on Huthwaite's observational research across tens of thousands of real sales calls. This drill is an original training adaptation of its published ideas.
evidenceType: Observational field research on recorded sales calls. Strong for large, complex sales; the original research found small-sale techniques did not transfer to big deals.
fits: Buyers who have a problem they have not fully sized
strains: Buyers who already know what they want and only need a price
coreMoves: Situation questions: learn the facts of the buyer's current setup. Keep these few; too many bore the buyer.
Problem questions: find difficulties, dissatisfactions and pain in the current setup.
Implication questions: explore the consequences of those problems (cost, risk, knock-on effects) so the buyer feels their size.
Need-payoff questions: get the buyer to say, in their own words, the value of solving the problem.
Present the solution late, and only against needs the buyer has stated. Pitching before diagnosing is penalised.

opener: Set a purpose for the call that invites the buyer to talk
Did not pitch features in the opener
discovery: Asked Situation, then Problem, then Implication, then Need-payoff questions
Kept Situation questions brief and relevant
Developed at least one problem through Implication questions before offering anything
Got the buyer to state the value of a solution in their own words
objectionHandling: Prevented objections by building value first rather than handling them after
When an objection came, returned to the buyer's stated needs and implications
close: Proposed a next step that matched the buyer's stated needs
Asked for a commitment that moves the sale forward (an advance), not just a vague follow-up

ethicsGuardrails: Implication questions must explore real consequences, not invent or exaggerate fears.
Do not put words in the buyer's mouth during Need-payoff questions.
